newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills one, wounds 13 in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills one, wounds 13 in Algeria.

text.p: A bomb exploded on Monday in a market in the Algerian town of Boufarik, south of Algiers, killing one person and wounding 13, Algerian state-run radio said, quoting a security forces statement.
The bomb went off at about 7:10 a.m (0610 GMT), it said.
Boufarik lies about 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers and has been the scene of previous bomb attacks that the authorities have blamed on Moslem fundamentalists.
At least 12 people were killed and scores wounded on January 16 when a car bomb ripped through a car market in the outskirts of Boufarik.

The Algerian newspaper Liberte on Monday reported that a bomb also exploded on Saturday in the Moslem stronghold of Medea, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers. There were injuries from the blast, said Liberte, without giving details.

Monday's bomb explosion came after Algeria's ruthless guerrilla movement, the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), warned in a statement by its chief Antar Zouabri that it would step up killings in Algeria with more massacres and bombings.
The statement was reported by the London-based al Hayat newspaper on Monday.

More than 300 people have been killed in massacres and bombings, mostly in Algiers and nearby towns and villages in the past month after a similiar warning from the GIA early in January that it would increase attacks.
At least 200 Moslem guerrillas have died in operations by the security forces in the past four weeks, according to Algerian newspaper reports.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
